macro.narrative: The expanding ISM manufacturing and services orders, coupled with a steepening yield curve and a bullish S&P, signal a broader economic upswing that should lift demand for TechnipFMC’s subsea solutions. This macro backdrop strengthens end‑market demand, pricing power, order backlog and capex, while the higher borrowing rates implied by the yield curve raise financing costs and commodity‑driven input costs.

implications.why: Higher ISM new orders and a bullish S&P point to stronger industrial activity, boosting demand for subsea infrastructure.
With demand outpacing supply, TechnipFMC can maintain or raise contract prices for its integrated subsea services.
The rise in new orders and client capex commitments expands the company’s backlog, improving revenue predictability.
Clients’ increased capital spending on offshore projects directly drives TechnipFMC’s project pipeline and revenue growth.
A steepening yield curve often signals higher commodity prices, raising material and labor costs for subsea construction.
The upward‑sloping 10‑year/2‑year curve indicates higher borrowing rates, increasing the company’s financing expenses.
